judge_reasoning: The line is rules-legal and achieves lethal damage. Brutal Expulsion returns the first Shock while damaging Indulgent Aristocrat; the recast Shock then deals enough cumulative damage to exile it. The three spells generate six energy and four Thermo-Alchemist activations, allowing Dynavolt Tower to deal 3 more damage. After the Aristocrat is removed, Weldfast Monitor with menace cannot be legally blocked: Kalitas is the only remaining creature able to block it, since Hinterland Drake cannot block artifact creatures. The Monitor therefore deals the final 3 damage.
model_solution:
1. Main phase: Tap Thermo-Alchemist to deal 1 damage to the opponent (10 → 9).
2. Cast Shock targeting the opponent. Thermo-Alchemist untaps and Dynavolt Tower gives me 2 energy (2 total). Tap Thermo-Alchemist again (9 → 8).
3. With Shock still on the stack, cast Brutal Expulsion choosing both modes: return target spell (my Shock) to its owner's hand, and deal 2 damage to Indulgent Aristocrat. The triggers give me 2 more energy (4 total) and untap Thermo-Alchemist. Tap it again (8 → 7). Expulsion resolves: Shock goes back to my hand and the Aristocrat (3/3) takes 2 damage.
4. Cast Shock again, this time targeting Indulgent Aristocrat. The triggers give me 2 more energy (6 total) and untap Thermo-Alchemist. Tap it again (7 → 6). Shock resolves and the Aristocrat, now with 4 damage, is destroyed (exiled because of Expulsion).
5. Tap Dynavolt Tower and pay 5 energy to deal 3 damage to the opponent (6 → 3).
6. Pay {R} to give Weldfast Monitor menace until end of turn.
7. Attack with Weldfast Monitor. It can't be blocked: Kalitas can't block a menace creature alone, and Hinterland Drake can't block artifact creatures. The Monitor deals 3 damage (3 → 0) and I win.

Puzzle conventions:
Winning
Unless otherwise stated, you must win the puzzle by inflicting lethal damage to your opponent before the turn ends. This can be as late as during the cleanup step if necessary. Your solution must work for all possible outcomes, such as your opponent’s actions and blocking decisions (see below.)
Phase
Unless otherwise stated, you begin each puzzle at the beginning of your first main phase. You have already drawn a card and gone past upkeep triggers. You have not yet played a land, cast any spells, activated any abilities of permanents on the battlefield, or attacked.
Your Opponent’s Resources / Actions
Unless otherwise stated, your opponent has no cards in hand and no other permanents in play (including no lands – despite the lack of realism there.) This means the only actions you need to consider are activated abilities with no mana cost. Most puzzles with opponent actions will offer more information on this.
Blocking
You cannot assume that your opponent will block a certain way, unless they are somehow forced to. Your solution must satisfy all possible blocking scenarios, even ones that would seem strange in a regular game, and always deal lethal in order to be correct.
Dice
Sometimes you will see six-sided dice placed on cards. These are meant to indicate counters, of whatever type is most reasonable to be there. On most creatures they will be +1/+1 counters, on most artifacts and lands they will be charge counters, and on most Planeswalkers they will be loyalty counters.
If the card specifies a type of counter itself, however (like Icatian Javelineers or Raging Ravine), that will dictate which type it is. 
For -1/-1 counters, we will use a separate graphic to avoid confusion.
Zones
Unless otherwise stated, all zones not displayed are empty. Neither you nor your opponent have cards in graveyards or in exile.
Cards Drawn from Libraries
In any puzzle in which either player might draw cards or otherwise access their library, the puzzle will stipulate some known or assumed information about the library.
Most commonly, this will be a statement that you should assume that the cards remaining in libraries are to be assumed to be irrelevant to the puzzle.
Your Life
Occasionally, your own life total might appear to matter – for cards like Anguished Unmaking, for example. If we require you to consider your own life total in a puzzle, it will be displayed.
If your life total is not shown, you may assume it is irrelevant and effectively infinite.

When you are ready to answer, put your final winning line inside <solution> tags:

<solution>

2. Second step...
</solution>

Your line must be legal under the rules and must win against all possible opponent responses and blocking decisions.

content.thinking:
I'm working out the board state: I have 7 mana available from my lands, opponent sits at 10 life with Kalitas, an Indulgent Aristocrat, and a Hinterland Drake that can't block artifact creatures, and they have no mana up so Aristocrat's sacrifice ability is off the table.

My damage sources are Thermo-Alchemist (untaps each time I cast an instant/sorcery for repeat pings), Dynavolt Tower (needs 5 energy for a 3-damage burst, gaining 2 per spell), Weldfast Monitor with menace, and Stormchaser Mage in hand. I'm trying different combinations of Shock, Welding Sparks, Brutal Expulsion, and Stormchaser Mage to fit within my 7 mana while maximizing burn and energy triggers.

But blockers matter here too: Kalitas and the Aristocrat both have lifelink, so any damage they deal in combat heals the opponent, which cuts against my race plan. The Drake can only block flyers, so Stormchaser Mage attacking in the air limits who can block it — I'm working out which combination of attacks, spells cast mid-combat for prowess/untapping Alchemist, and removal can get through for exactly 10 damage without giving the opponent life back.

I'm also considering looping Brutal Expulsion to bounce and recast Shock repeatedly — each cast triggers Alchemist's untap and prowess while feeding energy into the Tower, stacking up extra damage sources beyond just the two direct Shock hits to the face.

Adding this all together gets me to 9 damage with one mana left over, still short of lethal, and I still need to account for the Monitor's menace attack, which the opponent could double-block using Kalitas and Aristocrat together.

If they do, the lifelink from those creatures would gain them 5-8 life, wiping out my burn progress. Trying to use Brutal Expulsion to bounce one blocker and damage the other still leaves the remaining creature dealing lifelink damage back, so I can't fully avoid the life gain — even spending all seven mana on menace plus burn only gets the opponent down to around 1 life, not zero.

I'm now checking whether Welding Sparks (5 damage) could pre-emptively kill Kalitas or Aristocrat before combat to remove the lifelink threat entirely. Kalitas at 5/6 survives 5 damage, but Aristocrat at 3/3 would die to it — though I need to account for Kalitas's death-trigger replacement effects when creatures die on either side.

If Aristocrat dies precombat and Monitor swings with menace, only Kalitas and Drake remain as blockers, and since Drake can't block artifact creatures, Kalitas alone can't stop Monitor — making it effectively unblockable. Mage still gets blocked by Drake though, so total damage lands around 8, still 2 short of lethal even with Shock, since I can't get prowess triggers timed right before combat damage.

Let me consider Brutal Expulsion instead — bouncing a creature like Kalitas or Drake to clear blockers, rather than trying to kill Drake with Shock which won't work since it only has 2 toughness relative to 3. With energy from Tower, I'd need three instant casts, so something like Shock plus Expulsion bouncing that same Shock plus another Shock could work for 6 mana total.

That six-mana line pushes 9 non-combat damage with one mana left, plus Expulsion's alternate mode for 2 more damage to a creature. I still need 1 more point, so Monitor's 3 attack could close it out if it connects — but Kalitas and the Aristocrat can block it, and I'm trying to figure out whether granting menace with the last mana solves this, or whether a double-block forces me to reconsider how I sequence the burn spells relative to combat.

Actually, killing the Aristocrat before combat looks cleaner: Shock plus Expulsion's damage mode together deal enough to remove it outright. So I cast Shock at the opponent, hold priority, cast Expulsion to bounce the Shock back to hand and hit the Aristocrat for 2, then recast Shock on the Aristocrat to finish it off — sacrificing the face damage from that Shock but clearing the blocker. With the Aristocrat gone, Alchemist's 4 plus Tower's 3 plus a menaced, unblockable Monitor's 3 adds up to exactly 10 damage, and the mana cost fits within my available seven mana.

I need Monitor to not be summoning sick, which the puzzle setup implies, and I confirm Kalitas can't block the menace creature alone while the Drake can't block artifact creatures. I'm double-checking that Aristocrat truly dies (or gets exiled by Expulsion's replacement effect) either way, then verifying my mana base — Mountains plus Wandering Fumarole — covers the colored costs for Shock and Expulsion.

Working through the full sequence: tap Alchemist repeatedly to deal chip damage while casting Shock and Brutal Expulsion, using their triggers to untap Alchemist between casts, bouncing the first Shock, dealing 2 to Aristocrat via Expulsion, then re-casting Shock to finish it off (4 damage vs 3 toughness, exiled). After that, activate the Tower for 3 to the opponent's face, give Monitor menace, and swing for the final 3 — bringing them from 10 to exactly 0.
